question: As of April 2025, how many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists **22 recognized languages** as of April 2025.
 
• This schedule was initially adopted in 1950 with **14 languages** listed.
 
• Subsequent amendments, including the 71st and 92nd Constitutional Amendments, added **Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri**.
 
• The recognized languages include major regional languages such as Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Urdu, and Punjabi, among others.
 
• The inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule allows for their use in official communication, education, and legislative processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eighth Schedule Overview:**

 
 
• The Eighth Schedule is part of the Indian Constitution, which enumerates languages recognized by the government.
 
• It primarily aims to promote linguistic diversity and protect regional languages.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• The 71st Amendment in 1992 added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule.
 
• The 92nd Amendment in 2003 included Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali.
 
 
 
• **Official Language Policy:**
 
 
• Hindi, listed in the Eighth Schedule, is designated as the **official language of India**.
 
• English is used for official purposes along with Hindi under Article 343.
 
 
 
• **India's Linguistic Diversity:**
 
 
• India is one of the most linguistically diverse countries, with over **19,500 dialects** spoken as per the Census of India.
 
• The recognition of languages in the Eighth Schedule ensures government support for their preservation and promotion.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Recognition:**
 
 
• Recognized languages can be used in competitive exams, official communication, and legislative debates.
 
• They receive funding and resources for their development, including translation services and literature promotion.
